To: Claudia Zamora
From: Gerald Ibarra
Date: March 2
Subject: Fair contacts and follow-up order
Dear Claudia,
We came back from the two-day housewares fair at the Kelso exhibition center on Tuesday evening with forty-eight new contacts, the largest number any of our staff has brought back from a single event. The crates of display units traveled home on the same truck and have already been unpacked in the storeroom. A contact list that long means the trip paid for itself.
Our second production run of the lidded pantry containers is due to be completed on March 14, and shipments to distributors begin in that same week. Until then, only twelve demonstration units remain in the storeroom, and because one unit must be left with a customer at each first visit, the order in which we approach these contacts has to be fixed before the first calls are made. Please work through the contacts in this order:
1. Department store buyers who asked for a price list. Call these first, this week, and offer a demonstration at their store.
2. Regional distributors who took a catalog but gave no order estimate. Reach these second and ask how many units each of them would expect to take. The customer service desk is still logging inquiries from the fair, so keep your notes separate from theirs.
3. Independent gift shops. Write to these only after the distributors have replied and it is clear that demonstration units are still uncommitted.
Once all twelve units have been committed, place any remaining contacts on a hold list and tell them that a visit can be arranged as soon as the new units reach us.
Thank you,
Gerald Ibarra
Sales Manager, Gilford Housewares
P.S. Hugo Espinoza will have the contact cards from the fair typed into a single list by Thursday morning, so you will have everything in one place before the first calls.

For the next run, the second-floor zone should be divided between the North Stair and the East Stair, with the two halves starting a minute apart.

Y. T.

Brackenridge Energy Services
Workplace Energy Review
Brackenridge Energy Services carries out workplace energy reviews at no charge, showing businesses where their premises could use less gas and electricity.
To enter, send us the entry form with twelve months of meter readings, and we will confirm your place within three business days. Our survey team of two then spends one day on site, guided by a member of your staff. Four weeks after the visit, we mail you a written summary ranking the measures we recommend.
We can review premises only if their meters are registered in your name, not billed through a landlord or shared supply. You must also have occupied them for two years or more, and they must remain in use for a year after the visit. Each company may enter one property per round. Our team can also write an action plan on site for an optional $250.
Each round has its own entry deadline and review week:
Entries by March 6 — review week of April 13
Entries by May 1 — review week of June 8

From: Gavin Lindqvist
Sent: February 27, 10:12 A.M.
Subject: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
Copy: Site Services file
Dear Ms. Steadman,
Brackenridge Energy Services reviews one property per company in each round, so only one site can be entered this round.
I have checked our four premises against the published conditions. Gas and electricity at Netherby Road are included in the rent we pay the landlord, as they have been since we took that unit. Bramley Lane is metered in our own name, though we moved in last April. Vine Street has had its own meters for years, but the building returns to its owner in September. Torrance Park has been ours since 2016, its meters are in our name, and the lease there runs to 2032.
The entry form calls for twelve months of meter readings. For the site I have in mind, the earlier readings sit with our former billing agent, and the March cutoff is one week away. I would therefore aim at the following round. Should the optional action plan be included?
Gavin Lindqvist
Facilities Coordinator, Site Services
Talbot Packaging
Extension 2140
----------------------
From: Fiona Steadman
Date: February 27, 1:45 P.M.
To: Gavin Lindqvist
Subject: Re: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
File the entry against the March cutoff, not the later one. Our annual inventory count begins at Vine Street on May 18, runs through June, and will occupy this department, so the survey should be finished before it begins. Telephone the former billing agent's accounting office for the readings, which is quicker than writing.
This year's facilities budget carries nothing for outside consulting fees, so keep us to what the program provides. Once the entry has gone in, obtain written confirmation that our place is held.
F. S.
